title: silence-probe-reconnect-backfill-and-cancel-deadline-enforcement
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: Customers observed client disconnects that left server-side streaming state in a limbo where tool-calls were retried and KV-cache backfills were skipped, causing higher token costs and functional duplication. This PR introduces a 'silence probe' reconciliation path, a reconnect probe that attempts lightweight session health checks on client reconnects, an explicit cancel-deadline enforcement for in-flight tool/function calls, and safer backfill semantics when reconnect resumes. Summary of changes: 1) server: add silence-probe detection that marks streams as 'candidate-orphan' after configurable idle windows and enqueues a lightweight snapshot probe before evicting; 2) reconnect: on new client handshake include reconnect-probe phase which validates KV-cache continuity and replays missing prefix tokens if safe; 3) cancel-deadline: tool invocation subsystem now tracks cancel deadlines separately from client websocket state and enforces idempotent abort semantics with explicit response code for clients; 4) backfill behavior: when resuming, we prefer prefix-reconciliation over blind backfill and record a short reconciliation trace to observability; 5) OpenAI-compat: adapter layer now maps the reconnect-probe handshake into a 409/202-style flow when applicable and preserves function-call idempotency tokens. Implementation notes: code changes touch the session manager, rpc/stream controller, toolcall executor, and the OpenAI compatibility adapter. Default timeouts are conservative (idle->candidate-orphan = 45s, probe timeout = 5s, cancel-deadline grace = 2s) with knobs exposed in config. Tests: added unit tests for probe state transitions, e2e integration test that simulates abrupt client disconnect and reconnect with toolcalls, and property tests for idempotent abort on repeated cancel signals. Safety: probe performs non-destructive validation only and will not execute user-visible toolcalls during reconciliation. Rollout plan: feature gated via runtime flag 'streaming.silence_probe_v1' with spreadsheet of customers to flip; metrics added: stream.probe.started, stream.probe.success, stream.resume.reconciled, toolcall.abort.forced; alerting suggested on probe.failures > 1% over 10m. Backwards compatibility: existing client behavior unchanged unless server flag enabled. Related: follows ENG-4821 and references earlier streaming incident INT-998. Breaking change: none. See release_notes for end-user impact.
commits: 3 commits: 1) add silence probe state machine and basic probes (session manager + controller) 2) implement reconnect-probe handshake and prefix reconciliation; update OpenAI adapter mapping 3) enforce cancel-deadline in toolcall executor, add tests and docs
changed_files: server/session/manager.go, server/stream/controller.go, server/toolcall/executor.go, adapters/openai/handshake.go, runtime/config/defaults.yaml, tests/integration/stream_reconnect_test.go, docs/streaming-silence-probe.md, telemetry/metrics.yaml, Makefile
review_comments: Marcus: requested tighter metrics granularity around probe latency and suggested a separate probe_failure tag for tenant-scoped indexing. Elena: found a race in session eviction path when probe returns while eviction is already scheduled; asked for a test and small lock refactor. Samir: asked for clearer mapping of reconnect flow in OpenAI-compat adapter and an explicit 409 vs 202 decision table. Author replies: added metric 'stream.probe.latency_ms' and split probe_failure tenant tag, refactored eviction locking to use session-level RW mutex and added unit test, documented decision table in adapters/openai/handshake.go and docs/streaming-silence-probe.md. Approval: Marcus approved after metrics change. Elena approved after lock fix. Samir approved after docs update.
release_notes: Feature gated streaming silence-probe and reconnect probe which improves resilience after abrupt client disconnects. Adds cancel-deadline enforcement for toolcalls to avoid duplicated side effects. No behavioral changes until the runtime flag is enabled.
